page: Microsoft Azure E64-16as_v4 is a constrained-core memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the EASv4 series. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores (2 threads per core) powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz. While standard E64 configurations offer 64 vCPUs, this constrained configuration intentionally limits the compute thread count while retaining the full 512.0 GB of memory (32.0 GB per vCPU). The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, supporting standard instruction sets including AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2.

Hardware bundling includes 928 GB of local SSD temporary storage alongside the 512.0 GB RAM allocation, while operating without discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU throughput, reaching a stress-ng score of 2708.09, and a high PassMark memory score of 2811.33. Multi-core performance is balanced for its 16 vCPU footprint, registering 21661.1 on stress-ng multi-core and 9845.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 40.27 GB/sec, whereas write bandwidth measures lower at 22.75 GB/sec. Application testing shows 15.73 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a PassMark database score of 7033.19.

The constrained-core ratio provides a distinct cost-efficiency profile for enterprise software licensed on a per-core basis, such as relational database management systems. By reducing active compute cores to 16 while keeping the full 512.0 GB memory footprint, it lowers core licensing overhead while maintaining substantial memory capacity. Tradeoffs include lower raw multi-threaded compute and reduced write bandwidth compared to unconstrained compute nodes.

The Azure E64-16as_v4 is well tailored for enterprise relational databases (such as SQL Server or Oracle), in-memory caching systems, large-scale Redis deployments, and analytical processing engines where working sets demand vast RAM capacity without requiring heavy parallel compute core density.
